opps.title: 5 accounts stopped ordering — $1,309 of commission gone quiet
opps.body: Each of these bought from you last year and has ordered nothing at all in 2026. A lost account is the most expensive kind of decline: there is no brand mix to fix and nothing replaces it automatically — the whole relationship has stopped. The largest, NYX, was worth 405 cases last year on its own. These are the calls with the shortest path back to commission, because the account already knows you.

opps.title: Dante's — down 53% YoY
opps.body: Still ordering, but 566 cases lighter than last year (53%). It still does 507 cases a year for you, so the slide is worth about $566 in modeled commission. The drop is concentrated in Coors Light (-302 cases), Lite (-191 cases) — a mix problem you can work on the next visit, not a lost account.

opps.title: 8 accounts holding all year but soft this month — 194 cases behind
opps.body: Year to date each of these is fine, so the relationship is not the problem — but month to date they are all well behind where they were last August. That is the pattern that becomes a bad quarter if nobody catches it, and it is the cheapest kind to fix: the account is still buying, it just has not placed its usual order yet. Together they are 194 cases and about $194 of commission behind last August's pace, with days left in the month to close it.
